name: Brittany Kaiser

summary.text: Brittany Kaiser was director of business development at Cambridge Analytica until she left in March 2018 after about four years. She gave oral and written evidence to the UK DCMS Committee in April 2018 about the company's dealings with Leave.EU and Arron Banks, submitted further documents in July 2019, and in January 2020 was identified as the source of the @HindsightFiles release of internal Cambridge Analytica documents covering work in dozens of countries.

facts.claim: Kaiser, who left Cambridge Analytica in March 2018 after four years, told the DCMS Committee in April 2018 that she believed Leave.EU's leadership had combined data from UKIP members, Eldon Insurance and GoSkippy Insurance customers for analysis and ad targeting before the referendum.
facts.quote: Brittany Kaiser, who left Cambridge Analytica (CA) in March after four years, told MPs she believed Leave.EU leadership had combined data from Ukip members, Eldon Insurance and GoSkippy Insurance customers

sources.title: Misuse of personal data 'rife', parliament told

facts.claim: In written evidence Kaiser stated: 'In hindsight, I now think that there is reason to believe that misuse of data was rife amongst the businesses and campaigns of Arron Banks', and that if the Mississippi team had held or processed UK citizens' data in the US she believed that was likely to be a criminal offence.
facts.quote: "In hindsight, I now think that there is reason to believe that misuse of data was rife amongst the businesses and campaigns of Arron Banks."

sources.title: Written evidence submitted by Brittany Kaiser (FKN0076)

facts.claim: Kaiser's written testimony included a December 2015 email from Julian Wheatland to Leave.EU's Liz Bilney about a joint data programme for Leave.EU, UKIP and the insurance company, and stated that Arron Banks refused to pay Cambridge Analytica's phase 1 bill of £41,500 for work undertaken.
facts.quote: Arron Banks refused to pay our phase 1 bill of £41,500 for work undertaken

facts.claim: Kaiser told the DCMS Committee she had seen documents from Nigel Oakes, in charge of SCL's defence division, stating that the target audience analysis (TAA) methodology used to be export-controlled by the British Government, and that she understood the designation was removed in 2015.
facts.quote: she had seen documents from Oakes, the co-founder of the SCL Group, who was in charge of our defence division, stating that the target audience analysis methodology, TAA, used to be export controlled by the British Government.

facts.claim: In July 2019 the DCMS Committee published further submissions from Kaiser, including correspondence between Alexander Nix and Arron Banks; her cover letter asked the committee to reach new conclusions because earlier inquiries had found no work was done for Leave.EU.
facts.quote: a dossier of emails from Brittany Kaiser, a former Director of Business Development at Cambridge Analytica, of the communications between CEO Alexander Nix and Arron Banks

facts.claim: Beginning on 1 January 2020 an anonymous Twitter account, @HindsightFiles, began releasing internal Cambridge Analytica documents, starting with material on Malaysia, Kenya and Brazil; Kaiser was later identified as the person behind the releases, which were reported to cover work in at least 65 to 68 countries.
facts.quote: The release of documents began on New Year's Day on an anonymous Twitter account, @HindsightFiles, with links to material on elections in Malaysia, Kenya and Brazil.

facts.claim: Kaiser told the DCMS Committee that Julian Wheatland served as CFO and COO of Cambridge Analytica and worked under CEO Alexander Nix.
facts.quote: In the April 2018 session, Brittany Kaiser described Wheatland as CFO and COO and said he worked under CEO Alexander Nix.

connections.claim: Kaiser testified that Cambridge Analytica undertook phase 1 work for Leave.EU and that Arron Banks refused to pay the £41,500 bill; Leave.EU dismissed her evidence, and Banks' written evidence said Leave.EU told Wheatland it did not wish to proceed.
connections.quote: Arron Banks' written evidence says Liz Bilney subsequently confirmed to Julian Wheatland of Cambridge Analytica that Go Movement/Leave.EU did not wish to proceed.

openQuestions: The ICO's 2018 report found no evidence of a Cambridge Analytica–Leave.EU working relationship beyond an initial phase, and its 2020 letter described a limited amount of UKIP-membership-data work; Kaiser's account of unpaid phase 1 work and the 2019 Nix–Banks emails should be read against those findings.
The country count for the 2020 document release varies by source (65, 68 or 'over 60'); how much of the material was ultimately published is not established here.
Which written evidence number corresponds to Arron Banks' submission (cited here as FKN0056 from the search listing) should be confirmed on the committee site.
